title: Chronic Migraine as an Emergent Systems Failure: Integrating Upstream Neuroimmunology, Gut–Brain Dysregulation, and Computational Chronification
content: Chronic migraine affects 1–2% of the global population and is the leading cause of neurological disability in women younger than 50. Calcitonin gene–related peptide (CGRP)-targeting monoclonal antibodies and gepants represent the first disease-specific preventive therapies, yet in the registration trials in chronic migraine roughly six in ten treated patients still fail to reach a 50% reduction in monthly headache days, and medication-overuse headache compounds the problem. The therapeutic ceiling of single-target CGRP pharmacology suggests that chronification is governed by mechanisms upstream of, parallel to, and beyond the trigeminovascular neuropeptide loop. This narrative review synthesises converging evidence from 2020–2026 and proposes a multi-stratum model of chronic migraine as an emergent systems failure. In the trigeminocervical complex, the alarmin high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) is proposed as an upstream catalyst of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signalling to CGRP; in a nitroglycerin-induced chronic-migraine model in mice, pharmacological HMGB1 inhibition with glycyrrhizin attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity and reduced phosphorylated ERK, inducible nitric oxide synthase and CGRP release, though this is a single-laboratory result with a non-selective inhibitor. Clinical data from patients with medication-overuse headache reveal elevated circulating lipopolysaccharide, HMGB1, and HIF-1α, consistent with intestinal barrier failure feeding systemic neuroinflammation. Preclinical data on sex are contradictory and are reported here as such: a 2026 nitroglycerin model in mice found comparable hyperalgesia between sexes with male-predominant metabolomic disruption and male-restricted medullary TNF-α elevation, whereas separate work in rats found that sleep restriction with sub-threshold CGRP or PACAP produced allodynia in females only, with caffeine abolishing the male protection. The direction of sex-modulation in the gut compartment is unresolved; the human 3:1 ratio is not. Functional-neuroimaging synthesis implicates sustained decoupling of the salience, default-mode, and central-executive networks as the neural substrate of interictal cognitive impairment. A complementary computational perspective, grounded in the Free Energy Principle, conceptualises chronification as the formation of pathologically rigid prior beliefs — a hypothesis testable via task-based contingent-negative-variation, mismatch-negativity, and Hierarchical Gaussian Filter modelling of probabilistic-learning tasks. The review concludes that chronic migraine research must move from single-target optimisation to multi-stratum intervention. Priority areas include phase-1–2 trials of upstream neuroimmune modulation with mandatory immunological safety screening, sex-stratified microbiome trials, factorial designs combining sleep and network-level neuromodulation, and ethically calibrated priors-relaxing interventions. Establishing causality requires a longitudinal transitional cohort with integrated neuroimaging, electrophysiological, microbial, and ecological-momentary endpoints.
